aiOverview.content: St. John's University is a private, Roman Catholic, and Vincentian university founded in 1870, primarily located in Queens, New York City. Known for its strong liberal arts, business, and law programs, it emphasizes service, global education with international campuses (Rome, Paris, Seville), and Division I athletics (Red Storm). The university serves a diverse student body, focusing on academic excellence and urban engagement. Key Details About St. John’s University (NYC) Location: Main campus in Queens, NY, with additional locations in Staten Island, Manhattan, and Oakdale, NY. Academics: Offers over 100 undergraduate and graduate programs. Athletics: Competes in the NCAA Division I Big East Conference. Mission: Rooted in Catholic and Vincentian values, focusing on truth, service, and providing education to all. Distinct EntitiesIt is important to distinguish this institution from other schools with similar names: Saint John's University (Minnesota): A private, men's liberal arts college located in Collegeville, MN. St. John's College (Annapolis/Santa Fe): Known for its Great Books curriculum. Recent Highlights Basketball: The St. John's men's basketball team has experienced success under leadership, winning conference games in 2026. Campus Life: The university features modern facilities and easy access to Manhattan. Note: There is also a distinct St. John's College at the University of British Columbia (Canada) and at the University of Manitoba (Canada).
